comparison: Perfect agreement on task design validity (C65-C72, C36). Both evaluations strongly support the task design with OpenEval noting 'comprehensive description' and 'reasonable inference' for face validity, while peer reviewers praised it as 'clever,' 'compelling,' and addressing 'a great need for RL tasks that model threatening outcomes.'

Agreement on construct validity claims (C37-C38). Both evaluations support the construct validity argument despite small effect size. OpenEval notes 'appropriate acknowledgment' of limitations, while peer reviewers accepted the validity claim and noted the task shows promise for assessing state anxiety.

Strong agreement on core behavioral findings (C3, C20-C23, C51) and replication (C5). Both evaluations affirm the anxiety-avoidance relationship and its replication. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor with specific effect sizes, while peer reviewers consistently praised the finding and its successful replication across samples.

Agreement on computational mediation findings (C4, C27-C28, C42). Both evaluations support that reward-punishment sensitivity index mediates the anxiety-avoidance relationship. OpenEval provides detailed statistics, while peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the computational interpretation without challenge.

Agreement on reliability findings for most parameters (C6, C30-C32), but divergence on C33. OpenEval rates all claims as SUPPORTED including honest reporting of poor punishment learning rate reliability. Peer reviewers rate C30-C32 as SUPPORTED but express UNCERTAIN about C33, with Reviewer 3 noting it as 'the only real concern.'

Agreement on computational model validity (C24-C25, C64). Both evaluations support the model validation approach. OpenEval emphasizes model comparison, parameter recovery, and posterior predictive checks. Peer reviewers affirmed the computational modeling without questioning validation metrics, though OpenEval also addresses methodological claims C90-C92 not discussed by peer reviewers.

Divergent evaluations of experiential avoidance findings (C54-C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting 'honest reporting' of non-replication as a limitation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly noting the lack of replication 'may mean that this task is better suited to assess state anxiety' and expressing reduced confidence in psychopathology associations.

Divergent evaluations of sex differences (C48-C49, C59-C63). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting 'honest reporting' of mixed replication as exploratory findings. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 suggesting sex should be included as a covariate and noting the inconsistent pattern requires further investigation.

Divergent evaluations of practice effects (C34-C35). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing these as appropriately reported methodological considerations explaining poor test-retest reliability. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, grouping with C33 as part of broader concerns about punishment learning rate stability.

Divergent evaluations of punishment learning rate correlation (C26). OpenEval includes C26 in R4 rated as SUPPORTED with significant correlation reported. Peer reviewers separately evaluate C26 as UNCERTAIN, noting it failed to reach significance as mediator (p=0.052) and has poor test-retest reliability, raising questions about its stability.

OpenEval evaluated replication claims (C5, C46-C47) as SUPPORTED, noting demographic differences did not prevent replication and strengthen robustness. Peer reviewers discussed replication within R2 context but did not separately evaluate these specific replication and demographic claims.

OpenEval evaluated data quality and exclusion procedures (C78-C85) as SUPPORTED, noting transparent reporting and sensitivity analyses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological quality control claims.

OpenEval evaluated methodological rigor and open science practices (C73-C77, C86-C89, C94-C97) as SUPPORTED, noting pre-registration, validated instruments, power analyses, and data sharing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological claims.

OpenEval evaluated theoretical background claims (C1, C7-C8) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations establishing well-established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background literature claims.

OpenEval evaluated rationale for new task development (C2, C11-C14, C18-C19) as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inferences about limitations of existing approaches. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these rationale claims.

OpenEval evaluated literature review claims (C9-C10, C15-C17, C39-C45) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and discussion of inconsistent prior findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature review claims.

OpenEval evaluated descriptive and methodological details (C52, C93) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate specificity for context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these descriptive claims.
